en_US.title: Brine Canyon Density Ladder Guide
en_US.scanner: Brine ladder detected: layered density, false floors, sonar bend. Follow edges; avoid blind drops.
en_US.terminal: FIELD GUIDE: brine canyons are not just visual depth. They hide pressure boundaries, current shelves, resource pockets and scanner false positives.
en_US.audio: A canyon is a staircase if your hull can pay for each step.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Brine canyons make progression physical: the player learns density layers, hull limits, pressure failures and resource pockets before deeper routes open.
en_US.external_site: HECTON-8 treats depth as engineering geography. Brine canyons are route ladders, not decorative trenches.
en_US.field_note: Use the vane shadows like steps. Open water here is not empty; it is a bad reading waiting to happen.

en_US.title: Vent Forge Field Process Guide
en_US.scanner: Vent-forge chemistry active. Sample quality depends on pressure history, heat pulse and slow cooling.
en_US.terminal: FIELD GUIDE: vent forges cook sulfides, noble-gas pockets, ceramics and sealant precursors. A sample's route through heat and pressure matters more than its label.
en_US.audio: The vent did not make ore. It made a process you interrupted.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Vent forges make resources feel scientific: heat, brine, cooling paths and pressure history produce useful materials without magic ore logic.
en_US.external_site: Resource collection in HECTON-8 is grounded in field processes: vents, brines, ceramics, sealants and pressure history.
en_US.field_note: Do not lift a fresh lot straight into cold water. Let the vent finish the anneal or the shell will craze.

en_US.terminal: FIELD GUIDE: pressure glass records old tide stress. Atlas sealant follows those cracks because the cracks already describe the system's failure lines.

en_US.field_note: Do not grind the pretty edge. Follow the fracture map and cut from the dead side of the seal.
